tasks.short: Discuss security solutions with teams and management

steps.what: Discuss security solutions, constraints and tradeoffs with stakeholders

tasks.design: Keep the discussion led by the tester using checked findings in {DOCS}. The tester explains choices, listens to operational constraints and agrees next actions with stakeholders.
tasks.previous_blocker: A technical recommendation is only useful when teams understand and can act on it.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is needed for this conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving disagreement about risk, urgency and implementation effort.
tasks.human_edge: The tester recognises uncertainty, resistance and concerns that change the recommended approach.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in responsibility or time allocation.

evidence.claim: Security solution discussions depend on contextual explanation and negotiation; no labour reduction is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the discussion itself. Report preparation and finding documentation belong to their existing tasks and are counted once.
The tester brings checked findings and solution options from existing assessment work; stakeholders provide concerns during s1. No structured-input automation is proposed.
Use existing document and meeting facilities; no custom build or new recording process.
Zero incremental upkeep because the workflow adds no component or new recurring work.
research_questions: Are delays caused by missing decision rights rather than conversation duration?

already_counted.description: Explanation, listening and agreeing next actions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0. No conversation time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect stakeholder information for risk evaluation

steps.what: Collect stakeholder data and clarify risk context
Organise stakeholder notes into a source-linked risk brief

loop.purpose: Organise checked stakeholder information without resolving contradictions
loop.input: checked stakeholder notes and supporting references
loop.output: risk brief draft with attributed statements and open questions
loop.check: Check attribution, business impact, uncertainty and contradictions against the original notes
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; manually organise incomplete or disputed material
loop.why_not_simpler: Stakeholder descriptions use varied language and contain qualifications

steps.what: Evaluate risk and develop mitigation strategies

tasks.design: Keep stakeholder questioning and risk judgement with the tester. A bounded step in {DOCS} organises checked notes into an attributed brief, which the tester checks before developing mitigation proposals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes must be reconciled across people who describe the same dependency differently.
tasks.enabler_now: Constrained drafting can organise supplied descriptions while exposing missing and conflicting statements.
tasks.still_hard: Determining which stakeholder account is reliable and how business impact changes risk.
tasks.human_edge: The tester asks follow-up questions and chooses defensible mitigations.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less note organisation; risk decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a dependency discussion from stakeholder evidence
reach.learn: Business process mapping and control ownership

evidence.claim: Source-linked organisation of checked interview notes is plausible; the small time reduction is an unmeasured design estimate.

assumptions: Boundary includes collection, note organisation and risk interpretation; implementing mitigations is outside it.

Stakeholders provide responses and existing supporting records during collection, with no extra form or new unpaid data-entry task. The tester captures speaker, date, process, dependency, impact statement, uncertainty and source reference in s1; that work remains fully counted. Missing detail requires human follow-up.
Try native note headings and document templates before a model step. No automated risk score is produced.
unknowns: Whether stakeholders agree on business impact
research_questions: Does brief drafting save time after attribution checking and follow-up questions?

incremental.description: Maintain brief instructions and inspect sampled outputs

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R93 gives gross7 and net2 after5 upkeep. Range0-1% allows ambiguous interviews to erase most drafting gains; collection and risk judgement stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine policy changes needed to improve cyber security

loop.purpose: Express human-selected changes in existing policy language
loop.input: chosen changes, rationale and current policy clauses
loop.check: Compare obligations, exceptions, scope and responsibilities with the selected changes; detect unintended stronger or weaker duties
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; tester writes disputed clauses manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy wording and cross-references vary, while fixed replacement rules cannot preserve all qualifications

steps.what: Verify policy revisions and submit the update proposal

tasks.design: The tester decides the required changes and uses a bounded drafting step in {DOCS} to propose tracked revisions. The tester checks the exact proposal before handing it to the policy owner for the existing approval and publication process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy changes require careful wording and consistency with existing obligations.
tasks.enabler_now: A constrained drafting step can suggest wording from selected changes without deciding corporate policy.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing workable obligations and resolving conflicts with operations or other policies.
tasks.human_edge: The tester understands the control problem and recognises wording that cannot be implemented.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in clause composition; policy authority remains with the policy owner.

reach.task: Prepare a controlled policy revision package

evidence.claim: Drafting tracked policy revisions from human-selected changes is plausible, with unmeasured savings and full human meaning review.

assumptions: Boundary is the tester's policy revision contribution; corporate adoption and publication remain existing policy-owner work outside this boundary, with no savings or new transfer claimed.

The tester produces chosen clause references, intended changes, rationale, scope, exceptions and proposed responsibilities in s1. All authoring and capture are counted. Missing policy decisions return to s1 rather than being supplied by the model.
Use native tracked changes and policy templates first; a separate build is justified only if repeated drafting remains substantial.
Infrequent policy work must still bear its own upkeep allowance; no reuse benefit from other tasks is assumed.
research_questions: Does occasional policy drafting save enough time to cover upkeep and detailed meaning review?

already_counted.description: Choose changes and verify the submitted proposal

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and recheck policy examples

approvals.approved_version: Exact tracked policy proposal, rationale and recipient policy owner; edits void approval; this is not corporate adoption

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R91 gives gross9 and net3 after6 upkeep. Range0-2% assumes sufficiently repeated clause drafting; infrequent or contested revisions may yield no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess physical security of systems and devices

steps.what: Inspect server and network device locations for physical vulnerabilities
Assess temperature, vandalism and disaster exposure against observed protections

tasks.design: Retain site inspection and exposure assessment as human work. The tester records the judgement in {DOCS} and discusses facility concerns through the existing handoff.
tasks.previous_blocker: A record cannot establish the actual condition of doors, cooling, placement and local hazards.
tasks.enabler_now: No new component is proposed; existing records can inform inspection without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether protections remain effective under local incident conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The tester notices physical conditions and mismatches between records and the site.

reach.task: Connect physical exposures to system availability requirements

evidence.claim: Physical inspection and contextual vulnerability judgement remain necessary; no new labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is physical inspection and assessment, excluding facility repairs and detailed engineering design.

The facilities lead provides existing protection records before s2; the tester observes current conditions in s1 and reconciles records in s2. No new structured capture, monitoring or unpaid facilities task is introduced.
Use existing site access and document facilities; no custom automation.
Zero incremental upkeep because the existing assessment workflow is retained.
research_questions: Which physical exposures are missed by records but found during site inspection?

already_counted.description: Site inspection and contextual physical risk assessment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0. Physical inspection and exposure judgement are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Slightly less note organisation and policy prose; discussions and physical assessment remain human.
reach: Prepare controlled revision packages and explain operational security tradeoffs
role.ambitious_version: A tester who makes security recommendations understandable and workable for their owners.
